Collect fitted estimates, diagnostics and reporting tables

Source: R/api-results.R
mfrm_results.Rd

Combine a fitted model and matching diagnostics, intervals, predictions, or scores into a reusable mfrm_results bundle for mfrm_report(), plot(), and export_mfrm_results(). Start with summary(res)$decision, $triage, and $status; unsupported or unrequested sections remain marked not_available or not_computed.

Usage

mfrm_results(
  fit,
  include = "standard",
  response_time = NULL,
  response_time_data = NULL,
  response_time_facets = NULL,
  response_time_score = NULL,
  output = c("object", "summary", "tables", "html"),
  diagnostics = NULL,
  compute = c("auto", "never"),
  predictions = NULL,
  intervals = NULL,
  scores = NULL,
  comparison = NULL,
  response_diagnostics = NULL,
  calibration_intervals = c("none", "normal"),
  calibration_level = 0.95
)

Arguments

fit

Output from fit_mfrm(), run_mfrm_facets(), fit_mfrm_testlet(), or fit_mfrm_random_rater() (or an unambiguous long-format data.frame with Person/Score and recognizable facet names; native CML and comparison-only fits use their own summary() and mfrm_facet_intervals() methods).

include

Section names ("fit", "diagnostics", "tables", "precision", "reporting", "categories", "plots", "facets_fit", "bias", "misfit", "linking", "network", "apa", "response_time") or purpose presets ("standard", "publication", "validation", "facets", "bias", "misfit_review", "linking", "network", "gpcm_review", "all"). Two-family GPCM defaults to c("fit", "plots").

response_time, response_time_data, response_time_facets, response_time_score

Optional descriptive response-time column, source long-format data.frame, facet columns, and score column for include = "response_time".

output

Return format: "object" (mfrm_results), "summary", "tables", or "html".

diagnostics, response_diagnostics

Optional matching diagnose_mfrm() or mfrm_response_diagnostics() output, identity-checked and reused without recomputation.

compute

"auto" (default) computes requested ordinary diagnostics when omitted; "never" reuses supplied/stored diagnostics only and marks missing dependent sections "not_computed".

predictions, scores

Optional matching predict() or predict_mfrm_units() / score_mfrm_persons() / score_mfrm_random_rater() / format-6 score_mfrm_calibration() outputs.

intervals

Optional saved mfrm_facet_intervals(), mfrm_population_intervals(), confint.mfrm_fit() ("slopes"/"steps"), mfrm_curve_intervals(), bootstrap_mfrm_gpcm(), or mfrm_random_rater_intervals() object (or named list), identity-checked against fit without recalculating intervals.

comparison

Optional matching extended-model compare_mfrm() result.

calibration_intervals, calibration_level

For testlet/random-rater fits, "none" (default) or explicit "normal" fixed-facet/step intervals at calibration_level (0.95 default).

Value

Depending on output, an mfrm_results object, summary.mfrm_results, named table list, or mfrm_results_html object.

Details

Reading order and attached inference. Inspect overview, readiness, fit_readiness*, triage, status, plot_map, and next_actions in summary(res). Named intervals attachments expose dedicated plot routes (plot(res, type = "facet_<name>") or "gpcm_<name>") without altering Wright-map uncertainty. Two-family GPCM, corrected JML, testlet, and random-rater fits retain their estimator-specific tables, status flags, and plot maps ("calibration", "raters", "scores", "response_diagnostics", or mfrmr_model_maps where applicable). Exports and RDS archives retain participant identifiers without automatic deidentification.

See also

fit_mfrm(), diagnose_mfrm(), mfrm_report(), export_mfrm_results(), mfrmr_output_guide()

Examples

# Long-running workflow; run explicitly when needed.
# example("mfrm_results", run.dontrun = TRUE)
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Load the package and example ratings
library(mfrmr)
ratings <- load_mfrmr_data("example_operational")

# Fit these ratings; replace the data-loading line for your own analysis
fit <- fit_mfrm(
  data = ratings,
  person = "Person",
  facets = c("Rater", "Criterion"),
  score = "Score",
  rating_min = 1, rating_max = 4, category_policy = "preserve",
  method = "MML",
  model = "RSM"
)

# Build the fuller results object, including diagnostics
res <- mfrm_results(fit)
review <- summary(res)
review$decision
review$next_actions

# Draw the Wright map
plot(res)
} # }
